external_entities.name: colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague who signs in through the identity broker and uses applications.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
external_entities.notes: The text does not state a single location for colleagues; they sign in from wherever they are.

external_entities.name: franchise colleague
external_entities.description: A colleague from a franchise store who is vouched for by the franchise identity provider.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state where franchise colleagues are located.

external_entities.name: own devices
external_entities.description: Devices used by colleagues at home to sign in.
external_entities.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

external_entities.name: HR system
external_entities.description: The system that supplies overnight group membership changes and leaver information.
external_entities.source_excerpt: it comes from the HR system overnight

external_entities.name: identity provider
external_entities.description: The franchise identity provider that vouches for franchise colleagues.
external_entities.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
external_entities.notes: The text does not state which colleagues this provider is allowed to vouch for.

processes.name: identity broker
processes.description: Signs colleagues in, issues tokens, signs tokens, accepts franchise identity-provider sign-in, pulls HR changes, and writes sign-ins to the audit log.
processes.source_excerpt: Everything colleagues use signs them in through one identity broker.
processes.notes: The text does not state whether colleagues are asked for a second factor.

processes.name: application
processes.description: An application that accepts tokens and decides what a colleague may do from the groups in the token.
processes.source_excerpt: Every application takes that token and decides what the colleague may do from the groups in it.
processes.notes: The text does not identify the applications individually.

processes.name: store admin console
processes.description: An application on the corporate network that allows a holder of a store-manager token to change prices and void transactions for every store.
processes.source_excerpt: The store admin console is one of those applications. It also runs on the corporate network.
processes.notes: The console does not check which store the colleague belongs to.

data_stores.name: key store
data_stores.description: A store holding the signing key used by the identity broker to sign tokens for every application.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_stores.name: directory
data_stores.description: The identity broker's directory containing colleagues and the groups they are in.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_stores.name: audit log
data_stores.description: A log to which the broker writes sign-ins.
data_stores.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.
data_stores.notes: Nobody has written down what the log records or whether it covers the franchise route.

data_flows.name: sign-in
data_flows.description: A colleague signs in to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Colleagues sign in to it from wherever they are

data_flows.name: issue token
data_flows.description: The identity broker issues a token to applications for a signed-in colleague.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Once the broker has signed a colleague in it issues them a token.
data_flows.data_description: A token carrying the colleague's staff id and groups

data_flows.name: use console
data_flows.description: A colleague presents a token while using the store admin console.
data_flows.source_excerpt: If the token has the store-manager group in it, the console lets the holder change prices and void transactions.
data_flows.data_description: A token containing staff id and group membership

data_flows.name: keep signing key
data_flows.description: The identity broker keeps its signing key in the key store.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker signs tokens with a signing key it keeps in a key store.

data_flows.name: fetch public half
data_flows.description: Applications fetch the public half of the signing key from the identity broker to check token signatures.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Applications fetch the public half from the broker to check the signature.
data_flows.data_description: Public half of the token-signing key

data_flows.name: pull changes
data_flows.description: The HR system supplies group-membership and leaver changes to the identity broker overnight.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Group membership is not maintained there by hand — it comes from the HR system overnight.
data_flows.notes: The description also says the broker pulls the changes once a night.

data_flows.name: maintain directory
data_flows.description: The identity broker maintains its colleague and group records in the directory.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker keeps the colleagues and the groups they are in its own directory.

data_flows.name: write sign-ins
data_flows.description: The identity broker writes sign-in events to the audit log.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The broker writes sign-ins to an audit log.

data_flows.name: franchise sign-in
data_flows.description: A franchise colleague signs in through the franchise identity provider and the identity broker accepts that vouching as a sign-in.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Franchise colleagues do not have staff accounts with us; their own identity provider vouches for them and the broker takes that as a sign-in.

data_flows.name: vouch sign-in
data_flows.description: The franchise identity provider vouches for franchise colleagues to the identity broker.
data_flows.source_excerpt: their own identity provider vouches for them
data_flows.notes: The text does not state which colleagues the identity provider is allowed to vouch for.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network on which the identity broker and store admin console run.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The broker runs on the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: home
trust_boundaries.description: The home location of colleagues' own devices.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: including their own devices at home

trust_boundaries.name: franchise
trust_boundaries.description: The franchise environment associated with franchise colleagues and their identity provider.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: We also let the franchise stores in.

assumptions.assumption: The directory is confidential because it contains colleagues and their group memberships.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the directory contains colleagues and the groups they are in.

assumptions.assumption: The key store is confidential because it holds the token-signing key.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the key store contains a signing key used to sign tokens.

assumptions.assumption: The audit log is confidential because it contains sign-in records associated with colleagues.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the broker writes sign-ins to the audit log.
